site.name: Minecraft Server Manager
site.tagline: Free, self-hosted control panel for Minecraft servers on Docker.
site.description: Run modded and vanilla Minecraft servers from your browser. Modpacks pinned to exact versions, one-click backups, schedules, live map, player analytics. Free, open source, and your whole panel is one folder.

hero.eyebrow: Open source. Self-hosted. No paid services.
hero.title: Your Minecraft servers, one panel, zero bills.
hero.subtitle: Minecraft Server Manager runs every server as its own Docker container and gives you a control panel that rivals the paid ones. Modpacks, backups, schedules, live map, player analytics, crash forensics, all in your browser.

pillars.title: Built for people who run servers, not tickets

items.title: One folder is your whole panel
items.body: Database, worlds, backups, and the shared mod library all live under a single data folder. Copy it and you have migrated.

items.title: Every server is a container
items.body: Each server runs on the battle-tested itzg image with its own CPU and memory caps, graceful stops over RCON, and crash detection.

items.title: Modpacks stay pinned
items.body: Packs are locked to an exact version. Upgrades are explicit, previewed, backed up first, health-checked, and rolled back with one click.

features.title: Everything a server owner reaches for
features.intro: The full feature tour, from creating a server to sharing its live map.

items.title: Resource-capped containers
items.body: Create, start, stop, restart, rebuild, and delete servers with graceful RCON stops and automatic crash detection.

items.title: Guided creation wizard
items.body: Simple or Advanced mode, with every image setting explained in plain English before you pick it.

items.title: Live console
items.body: A WebSocket console with an RCON command bar, log filters, and one-click player actions.

items.title: Player moderation
items.body: Whitelist, ops, bans, IP bans, and teleports, online through RCON and offline through the JSON files.

items.title: Five registries in one browser
items.body: Modrinth, CurseForge, Hangar, SpigotMC, and GitHub Releases. Three of them need no API key.

items.title: Add by link
items.body: Paste a project page, a GitHub repository, a slug, or a direct jar URL. The panel identifies it.

items.title: Import anything
items.body: Modrinth .mrpack files, CurseForge exports, or your own zip of jars, every jar identified and compatibility-checked.

items.title: Checksum-verified downloads
items.body: sha512, sha256, sha1, or md5 verified before a file reaches the server. A mismatch never ships.

items.title: Shared mod library
items.body: Deduplicated by sha256 and hard-linked into servers, so custom mods survive pack updates.

items.title: Pick-mods-first solver
items.body: Choose the mods you want and get the newest fully compatible loader and Minecraft version.

items.title: Save-safe backups
items.body: Snapshots with retention classes, restore in place, and optional world shrinking to reclaim disk.

items.title: Cron schedules
items.body: Restarts, backups, and RCON commands on a schedule, with the next run shown up front.

items.title: Blueprints
items.body: Export a server as a portable recipe, import it anywhere, and get the same server back.

items.title: Crash forensics
items.body: Crashes are detected, parsed, and suspects named, with one-click mclo.gs sharing and automated insights.

items.title: Update tracking
items.body: New server, pack, image, and mod versions are tracked, with pre-update backups and one-click rollback.

items.title: Live map
items.body: One-click BlueMap, served through the panel's authenticated proxy.

items.title: Analytics and storage
items.body: Playtime, deaths, and mining scoreboards, inventory forensics, per-server disk usage, and enforced quotas.

items.title: Discord and chatbot
items.body: Webhooks with per-event toggles, plus an optional per-server chatbot with constrained in-game powers.

items.title: Public status page and API
items.body: Opt-in status pages, invite blocks, a generated client .mrpack, and a read-only token-authenticated API.

items.title: Users, roles, and 2FA
items.body: Admin, operator, and viewer roles with TOTP two-factor authentication.

screenshots.title: See it in action
screenshots.intro: Desktop and phone. The panel is designed narrow-first, so every page works on a phone.

items.dashboard: The dashboard: every server, player count, and recent activity at a glance.
items.wizard: The creation wizard explains every setting before you pick it.
items.overview: A server's overview with resource meters and quick actions.
items.console: The live console with an RCON command bar and log filters.
items.mods: Mods from five registries, filtered to the server's loader and version.
items.worlds: Swap worlds and manage files from the browser.
items.backups: Backups with retention classes and in-place restore.
items.schedules: Cron schedules for restarts, backups, and commands.

install.title: Install
install.intro: Pick the option that matches your host. Both give you the same panel.
reqItems: Docker Engine (Linux) or Docker Desktop (Windows, macOS).
Node.js 24 or newer for the from-source install. The Docker image bundles its own.
A few gigabytes of disk for server images and worlds.

docker.title: Option 1: Docker
docker.body: A pre-built multi-arch image is published to GHCR on every release. Grab the compose file, set one variable, and start.
docker.after: Then open http://your-host:25564. In Portainer or Dockge, paste the compose file as a stack and set DATA_DIR_HOST in the stack's environment.
docker.warning: The panel drives the host's Docker daemon through the mounted socket, which is root-equivalent on the host. Treat the admin login accordingly and never expose the panel raw to the internet.

source.title: Option 2: From source
source.body: Any operating system, including Windows and macOS with Docker Desktop.
source.after: Open http://localhost:25564. The first run walks you through a system check, your time zone, and creating the admin account.

install.nextBody: The getting-started guide covers first-run setup, creating your first server, and where everything lives.

items.a: Yes. The panel is MIT licensed and uses no paid services. Everything runs on your machine.

items.q: Does it work on a Raspberry Pi or another ARM machine?
items.a: Yes. The Docker image is published for amd64 and arm64, and the from-source install runs anywhere Node.js 24 and Docker do.
Everything the itzg image supports: Vanilla, Paper, Purpur, Fabric, Forge, NeoForge, Quilt, and modpacks from CurseForge, Modrinth, FTB, and more.

items.q: How do I move my panel to a new machine?
items.a: Copy the data folder. It holds the database, every server's world, backups, and the mod library. Start the panel on the new machine pointing at that folder.
Yes. The panel has admin, operator, and viewer roles, and each account can turn on two-factor authentication.

items.q: Does it need to be exposed to the internet?
items.a: No. Players connect to the game ports, not the panel. Keep the panel on your LAN or behind a VPN or reverse proxy with authentication.
Geyser and Floodgate can be installed like any other plugin or mod, and the panel exposes the settings they need.
The Discord server has a support forum and real humans. Bugs and feature requests go to GitHub issues.
